targets.agentsMd: AGENTS.md: the open format (Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code and others read it)

rules.rule_text: AGENTS.md is plain Markdown with no required fields and no frontmatter; use any headings.
rules.evidence: No. AGENTS.md is just standard Markdown. Use any headings you like

rules.rule_text: Place AGENTS.md at the repository root; in a monorepo add nested AGENTS.md files per package, and the closest one to the edited file wins.
rules.evidence: Create an AGENTS.md file at the root of the repository.

rules.rule_text: AGENTS.md complements the README: put the agent-facing details (build steps, tests, conventions) here and keep the README for humans.
rules.evidence: AGENTS.md complements this by containing the extra, sometimes detailed context coding agents need

rules.rule_text: Cover what matters to an agent; common sections are project overview, build and test commands, code style, testing instructions, security considerations, commit or PR guidelines.
rules.evidence: Add sections that help an agent work effectively with your project.

rules.rule_text: List the exact build, test and lint commands: the agent runs the checks it finds and fixes failures before finishing.
rules.evidence: Yes—if you list them.

rules.rule_text: Codex stops adding AGENTS.md files once their combined size reaches project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default; keep the file well under it.
rules.evidence: (32 KiB by default)

rules.rule_text: Codex concatenates files from the root down, so guidance in a nested directory overrides the root file; put team-specific rules in the nested file.
rules.evidence: Files closer to your current directory override earlier guidance

rules.rule_text: A project CLAUDE.md lives at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md and is shared through version control; personal preferences go in CLAUDE.local.md, added to .gitignore.
rules.evidence: A project CLAUDE.md can be stored in either `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

rules.rule_text: If the repository already has an AGENTS.md, start CLAUDE.md with an @AGENTS.md import and add only Claude-specific instructions below it, instead of copying the content.
rules.evidence: putting an `@AGENTS.md` import in a `CLAUDE.md` next to it

rules.rule_text: Instructions for one part of the codebase go in .claude/rules/<topic>.md with a paths: frontmatter list of globs; paths is the only field Claude Code reads there.
rules.evidence: `paths` is the only field Claude Code reads from a rule

rules.rule_text: A Cursor project rule is an .mdc file in .cursor/rules/; a plain .md file there is ignored.
rules.evidence: Project rules must use the `.mdc` extension.

rules.rule_text: Cursor rule frontmatter has three fields: alwaysApply (true: always included), globs (auto-attached to matching files), description (the agent decides when it is relevant). With none of them and alwaysApply false, the rule loads only when @-mentioned.
rules.evidence: the three frontmatter fields interact to determine when a rule is included

rules.rule_text: Keep each Cursor rule under 500 lines and split large rules into several focused, composable rules.
rules.evidence: Keep rules under 500 lines

rules.rule_text: Repository-wide Copilot instructions go in .github/copilot-instructions.md as natural-language Markdown.
rules.evidence: create a file named `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

rules.rule_text: Path-specific Copilot instructions go in .github/instructions/NAME.instructions.md with an applyTo frontmatter glob (several patterns separated by commas); excludeAgent: "code-review" or "cloud-agent" hides the file from one of them.
rules.evidence: The file name must end with `.instructions.md`.

rules.rule_text: Keep Copilot instructions focused and short: files over about 1,000 lines lead to inconsistent behaviour.
rules.evidence: long instructions files (over ~1,000 lines) can lead to inconsistent behavior

rules.rule_text: Do not add generic requests such as "Be more accurate" or "Identify all issues": they add noise.
rules.evidence: requests meant to generally and non-specifically improve behavior

rules.rule_text: Copilot code review does not follow links: copy the relevant information into the instructions file instead.
rules.evidence: Copilot won’t follow them. You should copy relevant info into your instructions files instead.

rules.rule_text: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md: longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.
rules.evidence: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file

rules.rule_text: Write instructions concrete enough to verify: "Use 2-space indentation", not "Format code properly"; "Run npm test before committing", not "Test your changes".
rules.evidence: Write instructions that are concrete enough to verify

rules.rule_text: Prefer actionable details: name the command, directory, library or existing example the agent should use.
rules.evidence: Name the command, directory, library, or existing example the agent should use.

rules.rule_text: Keep only what the agent could not work out from the code: how to verify work (exact test, typecheck, lint commands), misleading places in the code, decisions that are not in the repo, corrections already made twice.
rules.evidence: it only holds what Claude couldn't work out from the code itself

rules.rule_text: Do not duplicate rules enforced by formatters or linters, and do not copy whole style guides: the agent already knows common conventions.
rules.evidence: Don't duplicate rules enforced by formatters or linters.

rules.rule_text: Do not document every possible command or rare edge cases: the agent knows npm, git and pytest; keep to patterns used often.
rules.evidence: **Documenting every possible command**

rules.rule_text: Reference files instead of copying their contents, and say what to look for there; this keeps instructions short and current.
rules.evidence: Reference files instead of copying their contents.

rules.rule_text: Group related instructions under Markdown headings and bullets; short imperative bullets beat dense paragraphs.
rules.evidence: group related instructions under markdown headers and bullets

rules.rule_text: No two instructions may contradict each other: the agent may pick one arbitrarily.
rules.evidence: if two instructions contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily

rules.rule_text: A rule that matters for only one part of the codebase belongs in a path-scoped file (Claude .claude/rules with paths, Cursor .mdc with globs, Copilot .instructions.md with applyTo), not the project-wide file.
rules.evidence: Move instructions that matter for only part of the codebase into

rules.rule_text: A multi-step procedure is not a project instruction: move it to a skill and keep only facts needed in every session.
rules.evidence: If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase

rules.rule_text: Do not compensate with IMPORTANT or capitals: a rule that can never have exceptions belongs in a hook, deny rule or CI check, not in the instruction file.
rules.evidence: adding IMPORTANT probably won't fix it

rules.rule_text: Keep personal preferences out of the shared project file; they belong in user-scope instructions.
rules.evidence: Don't put your individual response preferences in a shared project file
